guideTitle: 6 Best Food Storage Containers for Leftovers in 2026
metaDescription: Six leftover storage sets compared on sizes, lid seals, nesting, glass versus plastic and piece counts, from JSCARES and Canfanni to Rubbermaid EasyStore.
introParagraphs: Leftovers are the everyday test of a container set. You need a size that fits half a casserole, a lid that does not leak into the fridge, and a stack that does not collapse when you open the door. The wrong set leaves you hunting for matching lids at 9 pm.

This comparison covers six distinct picks: the 52 piece JSCARES set with five rectangle sizes, the 40 piece Canfanni set with labels, the 18 piece Rubbermaid EasyStore, the Vtopmart 8 pack of glass, the GoodCook 10 pack and the Rubbermaid Brilliance Tritan set. We left out the other JSCARES 62 piece set, the Dealusy and the PROMOZE 50 pack because they overlap with picks already listed or with our meal prep guide.
We evaluated each set based on product specs and buyer feedback on its listing, not on a lab bench. Where a listing does not state a detail, we tell you to check the product page.

products.name: JSCARES 52 Piece Airtight Food Storage Containers
products.description:
The JSCARES 52 piece set covers nearly every leftover scenario in one box. It includes 26 containers and 26 lids, with ten rectangles in five sizes: two each at 50.7, 33.8, 16.9, 8.1 and 4.1 ounces, plus round containers. The listing says the upgraded food grade plastic is BPA free and safe for the microwave and freezer.

Pairs of each size give you flexibility: a big 50.7 ounce container for half a casserole and a 4.1 ounce one for a spoonful of sauce. The tradeoff is storage, since 52 pieces need a deep cabinet or drawer. The listing describes the set as stackable, but check the product page for the exact nesting plan and dishwasher guidance.

It is the choice for a household that cooks big and saves everything. Compared with the Canfanni at 40 pieces, it has more containers and a wider size range. Compared with the Rubbermaid EasyStore at 18 pieces, it offers many more small sizes.
products.bestFor: Households that save a wide range of portions.
pros: Five rectangle sizes from 4.1 to 50.7 oz
Microwave and freezer safe per listing
cons: Fifty two pieces need cabinet room

products.description:
The Canfanni set includes 20 containers and 20 lids, plus 16 reusable labels and a marker pen. Each lid has silicone sealing strips and 4 sided latches meant to keep contents sealed. The listing describes durable, BPA free, food grade plastic.

Labels are the practical difference for leftovers, because they let you write what a dish is and when you cooked it. That prevents the mystery container problem. The tradeoff is the four sided latch, which takes more effort than a snap lid. The excerpt does not list microwave or freezer limits in the visible text, so check the product page.

It works for families who want order in the fridge. At 40 pieces it is smaller than the JSCARES at 52, but it adds labels the JSCARES excerpt does not mention. Compared with the GoodCook at 10, it offers twice as many containers and a latching seal.
products.bestFor: Fridges that need dated labels and tight latching lids.
pros: Sixteen reusable labels and a marker
Four sided latches described as leak proof

Microwave limits not in the excerpt

products.name: Rubbermaid EasyStore 18 Piece Large Containers

specList.label: Storage
specList.value: Designed to stack and store easily

products.description:
The Rubbermaid EasyStore is an 18 piece set of large containers with lids. The listing says each container stacks easily when in use and stores easily when not, and the ridged lids are designed for sturdier stacking in the fridge and pantry. An extended lip gives extra support for handling.

The lip is a quiet convenience: you can grip a full container without pressing the lid. The tradeoff is information, because the listing excerpt does not give capacities, airtight claims or microwave limits. Check the product page for sizes and heat guidance before buying.

It suits a household that values easy storage over specialty features. At 18 pieces it is much smaller than the JSCARES at 52 and the Canfanni at 40. Compared with the Rubbermaid Brilliance, the EasyStore is built around nesting and stacking rather than a clear, latched seal.
products.bestFor: Easy stacking and grip when the fridge is crowded.
pros: Designed to store easily when empty
cons: Airtight and heat limits not stated

products.name: Vtopmart 8 Pack Glass Food Storage Containers

specList.label: Lid
specList.value: Removable silicone seals, 4 hinge snap locks

products.description:
The Vtopmart 8 pack is the glass option for leftovers. It includes four rectangles at 35.1, 21.6, 12.5 and 5 ounces and four squares at 27.1, 17.6, 10.8 and 6.8 ounces. The listing says the glass is safe for the oven, microwave, freezer and dishwasher, with a range of -4F to 752F.

The lids have removable silicone seals and 4 hinge snap locks, which the listing describes as preventing leaks and spills. Glass does not stain from tomato sauce, which matters for leftover pasta. The tradeoff is weight, and you should check the product page for lid heat limits, since plastic lids are not oven safe.

It is the set for people who reheat in the same dish. With eight containers it is far smaller than the JSCARES at 52, but oven safe. Compared with the GoodCook plastic at 10, glass is heavier but lasts through staining.
products.bestFor: Leftovers that go from fridge to oven in the same dish.
pros: Oven, microwave, freezer and dishwasher safe glass

products.name: GoodCook Single Compartment 10 Pack Containers
products.description:
The GoodCook set is a simple answer for leftovers. It includes 10 containers and 10 lids, each with a single compartment embossed with 4 cup volume markings. The listing says the BPA free containers are dishwasher, freezer and microwave safe, and stackable.

One size keeps matching easy, since every lid fits every container. The embossed marks help you see how much remains. The tradeoff is variety, because all containers are the same size, so a small side dish still takes a full container. The excerpt does not describe the lid seal, so check the product page for leak guidance.

It works for households that want few decisions. Compared with the JSCARES at 52 pieces, it is minimal. Compared with the Vtopmart glass at eight, it is lighter but may stain over time. The Canfanni adds labels the GoodCook lacks.
products.bestFor: Simple matching containers with a single size.
pros: 4 cup markings show what is left
cons: Lid seal details not in the excerpt

products.name: Rubbermaid Brilliance Tritan Food Storage Containers
products.description:
The Rubbermaid Brilliance containers are made of crystal clear Tritan, which the listing describes as stain resistant and odor resistant. The lids are airtight with secure latches, and the seal is described as 100 percent leak proof. The listing calls the containers lightweight, sturdy and suitable for everyday use.

Clear walls let you see leftovers without opening anything, and latches keep sauces from leaking. The tradeoff is that the excerpt does not give set size or capacities, so check the product page for the exact piece count. It also does not state microwave limits.

It works for leftovers that need a tight seal, such as soup. Compared with the EasyStore at 18 pieces, the Brilliance emphasizes a latched airtight seal. Compared with the Vtopmart glass, it is lighter, and compared with the JSCARES, it is a cleaner look.
products.bestFor: Saucy leftovers that need a clear, latched lid.
pros: Clear Tritan shows what is inside
Stain and odor resistant per listing
cons: Set size not in the excerpt

buyingCriteria.explanation: Leftovers come in odd amounts, so a range of sizes beats a stack of identical boxes. The JSCARES 52 piece set spans 4.1 to 50.7 ounces in rectangles, and the Vtopmart glass runs 5 to 35.1 ounces. Single size sets such as the GoodCook at 4 cups are simpler but waste space on small portions. Pick the range that matches your cooking habits. A good habit is to portion leftovers into the smallest container that fits, since less air above the food slows spoilage. With pairs of each size, the JSCARES lets you match a 16.9 ounce container to a lunch and a 4.1 ounce one to a few spoonfuls of gravy.

Soups and sauces expose weak lids quickly. The Canfanni uses silicone sealing strips with 4 sided latches, the Vtopmart glass uses removable silicone seals with 4 hinge snap locks, and the Rubbermaid Brilliance uses secure latches. Snap lids without a gasket are fine for dry food but riskier for liquids. Check the product page for the lid description. Before trusting a lid with liquid, fill a container with water, close it, and tilt it over the sink. A gasket plus four latches, as on the Canfanni, should stay dry, while a plain snap lid may weep at the corners.

Glass resists stains and handles oven reheating, as in the Vtopmart set with its -4F to 752F range. Plastic is lighter and more forgiving to drop, as in the JSCARES and Canfanni. Tritan, as in the Rubbermaid Brilliance, offers clarity with less weight. Think about whether you reheat in the container or only store. Think about your most common reheating step as well. If you often warm food in the oven, the Vtopmart is the only pick here whose listing states oven use, so the plastic sets would need a transfer to another dish.

A date on every lid ends the mystery container problem. The Canfanni includes 16 reusable labels and a marker pen, and the GoodCook embossed markings show volume. Without labels, write on masking tape. Most leftovers are best used within a few days, so a date is more useful than a clever lid. Labels stick best to a clean, dry lid, and removable ones such as the Canfanni reusable labels survive a wash cycle. Writing a date on masking tape works with any set, including the Rubbermaid EasyStore.

A crowded fridge needs containers that stack, and a crowded cabinet needs ones that nest. The Rubbermaid EasyStore is designed to stack in use and store easily, with ridged lids for sturdier stacking. The JSCARES at 52 pieces needs more room than the GoodCook at 10. Measure your shelf before you buy a large set. Nesting matters when the containers are empty, and stacking matters when they are full. A set like the EasyStore balances both, while 52 pieces of JSCARES will need a dedicated drawer or bin.

Reheating and washing happen every day. The GoodCook lists dishwasher, freezer and microwave, the JSCARES lists microwave and freezer, and the Vtopmart glass lists oven, microwave, freezer and dishwasher. Where the excerpt is silent, check the product page, especially for lid limits. Wash gaskets by hand if the maker suggests it. Remember that gaskets and lids often have lower heat limits than the container body. If a lid warps in the dishwasher, it will stop sealing, so keep a few spare lids or wash them on the top rack where the maker allows it.

faq.q: How do I pick the best size set?
faq.a: Think about the biggest and smallest leftovers you save. The JSCARES 52 piece set spans 4.1 to 50.7 ounces, while the GoodCook holds a single 4 cup size. If you cook varied dishes, favor a wide range. If you are unsure, start with a mid sized set and add containers as you learn which sizes you reach for. Most households find a few mid sizes get used far more than the extremes.

faq.q: Is glass worth it for leftovers?
faq.a: Glass is worth it if you reheat in the oven or hate stained containers. The Vtopmart 8 pack lists a range of -4F to 752F. The tradeoff is weight, and lids are still plastic, so check lid limits. For a mixed approach, many people keep a small glass set for oven reheating and a larger plastic set for everyday storage.

That depends on the food, so follow standard refrigerator guidance and label each container with a date. The container affects freshness, not safety. When in doubt, throw it out. Cooked rice and poultry deserve extra attention, so cool them promptly and refrigerate within a reasonable time.

faq.q: Can I put hot food straight into a container?
faq.a: Let it cool slightly first. Hot food can warp thin plastic and trap steam under a latched lid. The listings do not state hot fill limits, so check the product page. A short cooling period of ten to fifteen minutes on the counter is enough for most dishes before they go in the container.

faq.q: Are latching lids better than snap lids?
faq.a: For soups and sauces, yes, because latches press a seal around the whole rim. The Canfanni and Rubbermaid Brilliance use latches. Snap lids are quicker but less secure. A latch can also be harder to open with limited grip, so test the motion in a store or consider the easier flip style if hands tire.

faq.q: How do I stop containers from smelling?
faq.a: Rinse promptly and wash gaskets separately if you can remove them. Glass such as the Vtopmart holds odors least, and Tritan such as the Brilliance is described as odor resistant. Air dry fully before storing. Baking soda and warm water can also lift lingering smells from plastic. Sunlight helps, too.

faq.q: Do I need so many pieces?
faq.a: Only if you save many leftovers. The JSCARES at 52 pieces and Canfanni at 40 pieces are for larger households. A 10 piece GoodCook set or an 8 piece glass set is plenty for one or two people. Start with the set whose sizes match your fridge shelf and add another only if you run short.
